name: A06-goodbye-heard-in-full
notes:
The closing matters as much as the opening, and it fails differently: `end_call` firing while the last sentence is still being played cuts the goodbye off mid-word. The platform's transcript records the sentence in full — it was generated in full — so no layer that reads a transcript can see the truncation. Here the words have to be in the recording, which means they have to have been played. The wrap-up tools are asserted alongside it because a closing that sounds perfect while dropping `log_outcome` is the failure mode the whole closing gate exists to prevent, and the two are only worth grading together.

The pattern is the prompt's own two scripted closings — "Have a beautiful day, {{first_name}}" and "Take care, {{first_name}}" — and it requires the NAME on the end, which is what makes it a clipping check rather than a vocabulary check: those are the last words of the call, so they are the first thing an `end_call` racing the audio cuts off. An earlier version listed synonyms instead (goodbye, bye, take care, have a lovely day) and failed a run where the agent read the scripted line perfectly, because "beautiful" was not one of the guesses.

tools.recall_lead_context: {"summary_text": "Margaret, CA, trial day 3 of 7. Mood last 3 days: 4,4,3. Today's meds: Lipitor at 08:00, Metformin at 19:00."}
